question_text: Which of the following liquids is a bad conductor of electricity? (निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा तरल पदार्थ विद्युत का कुचालक (bad conductor) है?)
options: Tap water (नल का पानी)
Lemon juice (नींबू का रस)
Distilled water (आसुत जल)
Salt solution (नमक का घोल)
explanation: Distilled water (आसुत जल) does not contain any dissolved salts (लवण) or minerals, hence it lacks free ions (आयन) to conduct electricity.
distractor_rationale: Tap water, lemon juice, and salt solutions all contain ions that act as charge carriers, making them good conductors.

ai_context.learning_goal: Identify which liquids conduct electricity and which do not.
common_misconceptions: Students think all water is a good conductor.
ai_context.hint: Think about what is missing in pure water that is present in sea water.

question_text: During the electroplating of copper onto an iron key, to which terminal of the battery should the iron key be connected? (लोहे की चाबी पर तांबे (Copper) की इलेक्ट्रोप्लेटिंग (Electroplating) के दौरान, लोहे की चाबी को बैटरी के किस टर्मिनल (Terminal) से जोड़ा जाना चाहिए?)
options: Positive terminal (सकारात्मक टर्मिनल)
Negative terminal (नकारात्मक टर्मिनल)
Either positive or negative (सकारात्मक या नकारात्मक कोई भी)
It is not connected to the battery (इसे बैटरी से नहीं जोड़ा जाता है)
explanation: The object to be electroplated must be connected to the negative terminal (Cathode), so that positively charged metal ions are attracted to it.
distractor_rationale: Connecting it to the positive terminal would cause it to lose electrons and dissolve into the solution instead of receiving a coating. The other options are incorrect for a functional electroplating circuit.

ai_context.learning_goal: Apply knowledge of electrolysis to set up an electroplating circuit.
common_misconceptions: Students often reverse the connections of the object to be plated and the coating metal.
ai_context.hint: The metal ions in the solution have a positive charge. Opposites attract!

question_text: What happens when electric current is passed through a conducting solution? (जब किसी चालक घोल (Conducting solution) से विद्युत धारा (Electric current) प्रवाहित की जाती है, तो क्या होता है?)
options: Only physical changes occur (केवल भौतिक परिवर्तन होते हैं)
Only magnetic changes occur (केवल चुंबकीय परिवर्तन होते हैं)
Chemical reactions take place (रासायनिक प्रतिक्रियाएं (Chemical reactions) होती हैं)
The liquid completely freezes (तरल पदार्थ पूरी तरह से जम जाता है)
answer: Chemical reactions take place (रासायनिक प्रतिक्रियाएं (Chemical reactions) होती हैं)
explanation: The passage of electric current through a conducting liquid causes chemical changes. This process is known as the chemical effect of electric current.
distractor_rationale: While a magnetic effect might be observable in the wires, the liquid undergoes chemical decomposition, not just a physical or purely magnetic change. It certainly does not freeze.

ai_context.learning_goal: Understand that electricity can cause chemical changes in conducting liquids.
common_misconceptions: Electricity only provides heat or light.

question_text: Which process is used to protect iron from rusting by depositing a layer of zinc over it? (लोहे को जंग (Rusting) से बचाने के लिए उस पर जस्ता (Zinc) की परत चढ़ाने के लिए किस प्रक्रिया (Process) का उपयोग किया जाता है?)
options: Galvanization (गैल्वनाइजेशन)
Electrolysis (इलेक्ट्रोलिसिस)
Smelting (प्रगलन)
Condensation (संघनन)
explanation: Galvanization is a specific type of electroplating where a protective layer of zinc is coated over iron to prevent rusting.
distractor_rationale: Electrolysis is the broader principle. Smelting is extracting metal from ore. Condensation is the change from gas to liquid.

ai_context.learning_goal: Identify practical applications of electroplating like galvanization.
common_misconceptions: Students may confuse galvanization with general painting or oiling.
ai_context.hint: It is a process specifically involving Zinc.

question_text: Why is a small amount of acid or base added to water before passing electric current through it? (विद्युत धारा प्रवाहित करने से पहले पानी में थोड़ी मात्रा में अम्ल (Acid) या क्षार (Base) क्यों मिलाया जाता है?)
options: To make it pure (इसे शुद्ध बनाने के लिए)
To make it a better conductor of electricity (इसे विद्युत का बेहतर सुचालक (Good conductor) बनाने के लिए)
To change its color (इसका रंग बदलने के लिए)
To make it freeze easily (इसे आसानी से जमाने के लिए)
answer: To make it a better conductor of electricity (इसे विद्युत का बेहतर सुचालक (Good conductor) बनाने के लिए)
explanation: Pure water is a poor conductor. Adding acid or base provides free ions, which significantly increases its electrical conductivity.
distractor_rationale: It makes the water impure, not pure. It does not change the color fundamentally or affect the freezing point as its primary purpose here.

ai_context.learning_goal: Understand how adding impurities like acids or bases increases conductivity by providing ions.
common_misconceptions: Adding acid makes it unsafe, so it shouldn't be done.
ai_context.hint: What is missing in pure water that allows electricity to flow?
